observations: Photo 0: a dusty, oil-stained automatic transmission/gearbox unit sitting on a workshop floor, showing bell housing, solenoid/sensor wiring, and a starter motor-like component.
Photo 1: close-up of wiring harness connectors and a sensor plug on the same gearbox, heavily grimed.
Photo 2: side/rear view of the gearbox showing the torque converter bell housing and bolt pattern, no tag or label visible.
No manufacturer plate, part number sticker, or VIN/part tag is legible in any photo.
No video or audio clip is provided to support 'tested and working' or 'no knock' claims.
Watermark 'GOD OF ABRAHAM INVESTMENT' overlays all photos; no vehicle fitment info given in images.

claims.evidence: No shipping label, customs tag, or import documentation visible in any photo.
No test bench video, fluid check, or diagnostic readout shown; only static photos of the unit.
This is an audio/operational claim; no video with sound provided.
No odometer, service sticker, or donor-vehicle paperwork shown.
Bolt heads and casing seams are too dirty/obscured in photos 0-2 to check for tool marks or re-sealant residue.

risks.risk: Vehicle fitment/model unknown, which is the primary price driver for a gearbox
risks.proof: Clear photo of the part number/casting tag or a photo of the donor vehicle's badge/VIN plate
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all; fitment-based price range is unknown

risks.risk: Internal wear (clutch packs, mechatronic unit, torque converter) cannot be assessed from exterior photos
risks.proof: Video of unit running on a test stand or bench, showing smooth engagement and no slipping
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / worst case

risks.risk: Fluid leaks or seal damage not visible under heavy grime
risks.proof: Close-up photo of seals and pan gasket after cleaning

risks.risk: Actual mileage/condition of donor vehicle unverifiable
risks.proof: Photo of donor vehicle odometer or import customs paperwork

risks.risk: Possible prior opening/repair hidden by dirt
risks.proof: Clean, well-lit photo of all casing bolts and seams

proof_requests: Photo of the part number/casting tag on the gearbox casing clearly readable, or the donor vehicle's make/model/VIN plate
A video clip of the gearbox running on a test bench with audible sound (to check for knocking)
Clean, well-lit photos of the casing bolts/seams to check for signs of prior opening
Any import/customs documentation showing origin (Belgium) and tokunbo status
response.reason: The gearbox's vehicle fitment/model, which sets its price category, cannot be read from any photo, and no supporting video exists for the 'tested and working' or 'no knock' claims, so even a worst-case price cannot be assigned without this missing identification.
